# Display Interface — GFX HAT

## Overview

The operator interface is implemented with a **Pimoroni GFX HAT** connected to the Raspberry Pi. The board provides:

- a 128 × 64 monochrome LCD;
- six capacitive touch buttons;
- RGB backlighting;
- six button indicator LEDs.

The interface is controlled by the integrated script:

```text
gfxhat_pattern_ui_usb.py
```

This script no longer acts only as a display demonstration: in real mode it selects the PNG pattern, opens the USB serial port to the ESP32, sends colour commands and updates progress when the ESP32 reports a microswitch event.

## Screens and Buttons

### Pattern Selection

```text
SELEZIONA PNG
> cuore.png
  righe.png
  fiore.png
^v SPOSTA  OK SEL  + REF
```

| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| `UP` | Previous PNG file |
| `DOWN` | Next PNG file |
| `SELECT` | Confirm selected pattern |
| `PLUS` | Refresh USB file list |

### Yarn Preparation

```text
PATTERN SELEZIONATO
cuore.png

INSERIRE
I FILATI

+ AVVIA    < MENU
```

`PLUS` starts the real processing sequence; `BACK` returns to pattern selection.

### Running State

```text
cuore.png
IN LAVORAZIONE

[ progress bar ]

36%   18/50
- STOP
```

In real mode the counter advances when the ESP32 sends `NEXT` after a microswitch press.

### Stopped and Completed States

The operator can pause the colour-selection mechanism with `MINUS`, resume with `PLUS`, or return to the menu with `BACK`. At the end of the pattern the completion screen is displayed.

## Application States

| State | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `SELECT_FILE` | Lists `.png` files available on the mounted USB drive |
| `INSERT_YARNS` | Requests the operator to prepare yarns before actuation |
| `RUNNING` | Displays the real progress of the selected pattern |
| `STOPPED` | Keeps the current pattern position while servos are released |
| `ALERT` | Prepared screen for an error or yarn-cut request |
| `DONE` | Reports successful completion |

## USB Pattern Selection

The PNG files are stored directly in the root folder of the USB flash drive. In the current setup, the drive is mounted at:

```text
/mnt/pattern_usb
```

When a pattern is selected, it is copied locally to:

```text
~/automated_knitting_machine/patterns/current_pattern.png
```

## Running the Display

### Demo Mode

Demo mode tests the UI without moving the motors:

```bash
source /home/aless/venvs/uncinetto/bin/activate
python3 /home/aless/gfxhat_pattern_ui_usb.py --usb-dir /mnt/pattern_usb --demo
```

### Real Mode

Real mode communicates with the ESP32, detected in the tested setup at `/dev/ttyUSB0`:

```bash
source /home/aless/venvs/uncinetto/bin/activate
python3 /home/aless/gfxhat_pattern_ui_usb.py --usb-dir /mnt/pattern_usb --port /dev/ttyUSB0
```

## Compatibility Note: LCD Contrast

During initial tests the installed `gfxhat` library did not expose `lcd.contrast()`. The robust display initialization is:

```python
lcd.clear()
if hasattr(lcd, "contrast"):
    lcd.contrast(42)
self.set_backlight((0, 40, 70))
```

This allows the program to run with library versions that do not implement the contrast method.

## Future Alert Integration

The interface already includes screens for:

- `ERRORE RISCONTRATO`;
- `TAGLIARE IL FILO`.

The visual error-recognition algorithm is documented in [Error Recognition](error-recognition.qmd). Connecting its output to the real actuator pause command remains an integration task.
